transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
I came in because most days I just feel like I’m at the bottom of a dark hole. Even when I’m around people I know, there’s this heavy, hopeless feeling that I can’t shake.
How long have you been feeling this way—days, weeks, months, or longer?
About a year and two months now. It started after I fell at the HVAC job and hurt my back—after that, everything just started unraveling.
Since this started after your accident, has this low, hopeless feeling been present nearly every day without a break, or have there been stretches of days or weeks where your mood returned to normal?
It’s been there most days. I don’t really get back to feeling normal—I just feel heavy and hopeless, like I’m stuck at the bottom of a dark hole.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days or more where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, or felt like your thoughts were racing?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything like that.
During this past year, have you lost interest or pleasure in almost everything you used to enjoy, nearly every day?

Yeah. I used to love hiking, painting, going to the makerspace, even figuring out a difficult install at work. Now I just look at the supplies or ignore people’s calls. None of it feels worth starting.
Before this past year, had you ever gone through a separate period—lasting two weeks or more—where you felt similarly depressed or lost interest in things, followed by a return to your normal mood?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of a separate time like that before this past year.
Over this past year, have you also noticed changes in your sleep or appetite—like sleeping much more or less than usual, or a significant change in your weight or appetite?

My sleep’s been all over the place. Some nights I lie awake for hours, my back hurting and bills running through my head. Other times I sleep half the day and still wake up feeling like I didn’t rest at all.
Have you been experiencing feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, trouble concentrating, or thoughts about death or suicide during this past year?

Yeah. I keep telling myself I’m useless because I can’t work like I used to. I replay every apprentice I feel like I let down, and every unpaid bill, over and over—it feels like proof I’ve ruined everything.

Thinking back further, did you notice any ongoing low mood or loss of interest going back more than two years, even before your back injury, or did this really start with the accident about 14 months ago?
It really started after the fall at that HVAC job. That was about a year and two months ago, and it feels like everything’s been unraveling since the back injury.
During this past year, have you noticed a loss of energy or feeling tired all the time, or trouble concentrating on tasks, nearly every day?

Yeah. The paperwork and repair diagrams that used to be second nature just blur together now. I’ll sit there and get stuck on something stupid, like which form I’m supposed to open first, and I can’t make myself decide.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a single, continuous depressive episode of about 14 months duration marked by pervasive low/hopeless mood, near-total anhedonia, sleep disturbance (insomnia and hypersomnia), fatigue, concentration difficulties, and feelings of worthlessness/guilt. No history of prior discrete depressive or manic/hypomanic episodes, making this a single episode rather than recurrent MDD. Onset temporally follows a physical injury/psychosocial stressor (work accident), but the severity, persistence, and breadth of symptoms exceed what would be expected for an adjustment disorder, and there is no evidence the mood disturbance is directly physiologically caused by the injury itself (e.g., no cognitive/medical findings suggesting an organic mood disorder), making F06.31 less likely. Absence of manic/hypomanic symptoms rules out bipolar spectrum diagnoses. Given the unspecified severity and lack of psychotic features, F32.9 (Major Depressive Disorder, single episode, unspecified) is the most accurate code.
